I am old now, 80 years, and my strength is not what it was. This small plot behind the house, less than half a plot, I plant my cassava and cocoyam together as I have always done. I cannot buy the chemical fertilizer — it is too dear and the government one never reaches us here. I use the kitchen ash and the goat droppings from my small pen, that is what feeds the soil. My grandchildren help me when they come from school, and sometimes I pay a young man small money to help clear the bush before planting.
